summary: Kept the form, relief and massing. Raised the stone and slate wear in the age step (`age.rules`, run by `make.sh`) from moderate/light to heavy, which writes 86 cells instead of 38. It adds mossy and worn stone brick and tuff on the plinth, walls and gate, plus cobbled deepslate and tuff patches on the roof. `mcd check` shows 0 floating and 0 orphan blocks, and `mcd palette` shows no flags. I rendered the front-left, front-right, front-elevation and back-elevation views; I did not render the left and right elevations or the street views. The age is visible but modest.
applied: Add visible age: `weather heavy` on the stone brick and deepslate tile walls, plus `weather moderate` and `vary subtle` on the slate roof. This gives mossy cobblestone, mossy stone brick, tuff brick and cobbled deepslate in separated patches, with moss kept low. The reviewers saw no weathering at all on the previous version.

Fewer colour families: the new worn blocks are grey and green-grey (tuff, moss, cobbled deepslate) and sit inside the existing stone and slate families. The earlier cuts of gold, red and yellow stay, so no new family was added.
skipped: Restyling the pink, blue and verdigris accents to cut colour families further: these are the polychrome identity of a painted lady, and cutting them would lose the 'Victorian house with turret' reading.
Weathering the blue concrete-powder body: it has no worn variant, and a freshly painted body suits the style. The age sits on the stone and roof only.
Cracked stone brick and cracked deepslate variants: the toolkit skipped them as invisible at render size.
Vines, a new age material: not added, because they would add a green family against the request for fewer colour families.
